nl_dino_s_bluff.blurb: A sport crag on the Avalon Peninsula near Avondale and Conception Harbour, under an hour's drive from St. John's. The rock is volcanoclastic, and the main face looks south. Its left end is ledgy slab climbing, and around the corner the wall steepens into thin vertical faces and overhangs, finishing in a large recess with roofs, corners and arêtes. The 16 sport routes run from easy 5.7 up to 5.14, but most sit between 5.10 and 5.13, so it suits strong climbers more than beginners, though a few moderates exist on the slabby side. The walk to the base is short, and the northern base has more walls that have yet to be developed.

nl_first_bay.blurb: A small bouldering bay at Blackhead, just outside St. John's on the Avalon Peninsula, with boulders sitting beneath a big cliff close to the water. The stone is solid and the problems are good, though blocks have been known to move over winter, so check landings after the cold months. Thirteen problems are recorded, with the bulk around V2, a couple near V4, and a handful of much harder lines reaching into the upper grades, including one at V11. A walk-in along the coast and a short scramble down gets you in. The next cove along holds many more boulders.

nl_random_boulders.blurb: A scatter of boulders in Birthday Cove at Blackhead, on the coast near St. John's on the Avalon Peninsula. There are 16 problems, and the grade spread leans easy: about half are VB to V1, with a few around V3 and a couple of harder ones up to the V6 range. Problems are short, with balance-and-weight-shift style movement on some of them, and one sits up by the rappel. Because the boulders are by the ocean, the rock can turn slippery when wet or damp, and tree roots poke out near some landings, so bring a pad and a spotter.
